pains.title: Paying dietitians: employee, contractor and the split
pains.problem: The label in the agreement does not decide 1099 status. The IRS, and some stricter states, look at control over schedule, fees and systems.
pains.how: Lucid reviews how each dietitian is paid against those factors and models what a split, hourly rate or salary does to your margin. Close calls go to your attorney.

pains.title: Busy schedule, thin profit
pains.problem: A group splits every fee with the dietitian, then pays for software, billing help and staff. Insurance pays a small amount per 15 minute unit.
pains.how: Lucid builds a profit view by dietitian and by payer, with break even caseload and the cost of a new hire while credentialing is pending.

pains.title: Packages, superbills and refunds
pains.problem: Packages bring cash in before sessions happen, so collected money is often not earned revenue yet. Refunds and expired sessions complicate it.
pains.how: Lucid reports package revenue as sessions are delivered, keeps refunds and no-show fees on their own lines and separates cash pay from insurance revenue. Your CPA sets the method that fits your tax basis.

faq_title: Dietitian practice accounting questions owners ask

faq.q: Can I pay my dietitians as 1099 contractors in my group practice?
faq.a: It depends on how much control you have over their work, not on the label in the agreement, and some states apply stricter tests than the IRS. If you set schedules, fees and systems, they may be employees. Lucid reviews how each dietitian is paid and models the cost of each pay setup, and your attorney confirms the legal side.

faq.q: How do I know if taking insurance is actually profitable for my dietitian practice?
faq.a: Compare what each payer pays per visit with what that visit costs you in dietitian pay, software and admin time. Lucid sets up your books by payer and by dietitian so that number is clear every month. Then you can decide which plans to keep, ask for better rates or limit.

faq.q: Why is my dietitian practice short on cash in January and February?
faq.a: Plans reset and many claims are denied or held for benefit checks, so payments slow just as new year bills start. Lucid's cash flow forecast shows the dip coming, with payer mix tracking. Your biller or billing software handles the claim fixes.

faq.q: Do I owe taxes in other states if my dietitians see clients by telehealth?
faq.a: Possibly. A few states tax counseling fees or gross receipts, and several tax digital products or paid group sessions. Lucid tracks your revenue by client state, and your CPA tells you where filings may be needed.

faq.q: Do I need to charge sales tax on supplements or meal plans I sell?
faq.a: It depends on your state and the product. Counseling is often not taxed, but supplements, downloads and subscriptions can be. Lucid books product sales separately and tracks sales tax by state, and your CPA checks what applies to you.
